clue.text: Drinks outlet belonging to criminal left in charge inside

parts.note: of expresses belonging, as in 'the house of my father'

indicators.note: placed inside means the left-in-charge letters sit within the word for the criminal

parts.note: a fence is a criminal who receives and sells stolen goods

explanation.surface: A shop selling drink turns out to be owned by a crook who has put someone in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: An off-licence is a British shop licensed to sell alcohol for drinking elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the shop that sells alcohol to take away is named for its licence to sell off the premises.

clue.text: Head ignoring bishop previously

indicators.note: ignoring the bishop means that letter is left out of the word for head

parts.note: bonce is British slang for the head
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a head who used to pay no attention to the bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happened at one time in the past happened formerly, a straight synonym.

clue.text: College student, one that was bound over, supported by that woman

indicators.note: in a down entry, supported by means the second piece sits beneath the first
in a down clue, over means the word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a serf was a medieval labourer bound to the land
her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: A student appears to have been bound over to keep the peace, with a woman backing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound over' looks like the legal phrase; here 'one that was bound' is a serf and 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A first-year at a British college or university is commonly called by this informal name.

clue.text: Financing IT is reviewed as very minor

indicators.note: reviewed suggests the letters are looked at again and reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A finance review concludes that the IT spend is trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of negligible importance or size is trivial, matching very minor.

clue.text: Trio in establishment going to shooting venue drive apart

indicators.note: going to means the next piece joins on after the first
a trio in the word establishment means its opening three letters are taken

parts.note: a range is a place for target shooting

explanation.surface: Three people from an institution head to a firing range and fall out.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate people is to push them apart emotionally, so drive apart is a direct paraphrase.

clue.text: Making use of a deck, get plastered

indicators.note: making use of the words suggests they are reworked, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A card player using the pack gets drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastered' suggests drunk; here it means thickly coated, as with mud.
explanation.definitionFit: Covered in a thick crust, as boots with mud, is the coated sense of plastered.

clue.text: Report of star not working

indicators.note: report of signals a word as spoken, giving its sound-alike

parts.note: a star, a much-adored celebrity, is an idol

explanation.surface: News of a celebrity who is out of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Inactive or unemployed things or people are described as lying unused, the same sense as not working.

clue.text: Companion in action on stage getting old money

indicators.note: in places the companion's letters inside the word for stage action

parts.note: drama is action performed on stage
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A companion in a play is rewarded with old cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek currency before the euro, so a former unit of money.

clue.text: Field uniform designed for the inexperienced?

parts.note: the field in a race or competition is its entry, those taking part
uniform as in even or consistent means level

explanation.surface: Army field uniform made for raw recruits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field uniform' reads as battledress; the two words split into separate synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: Products or jobs pitched at beginners are described as basic, suited to novices.

clue.text: Cases in which time is lost in game

indicators.note: is lost means the letter for time drops out of the word for cases

parts.note: chests are cases or boxes

explanation.surface: Legal cases where the clock runs out during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A board game for two players with kings, queens and pawns.

clue.text: Carry off bit of a brightly-coloured suit in rally

parts.note: to carry off is to take
hearts is a red suit in a pack of cards, and one card of it is a heart

explanation.surface: Someone at a rally makes off with part of a garish outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'suit' is a card suit, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally is to recover courage or spirits, which is the idiom meaning to be encouraged.

clue.text: Shock line to interrupt antisocial behaviour? It characterises fusspots

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass of it

indicators.note: to interrupt means the letter for line breaks into the word for the behaviour

parts.note: spitting in public is antisocial behaviour

explanation.surface: A shock interrupts some rude conduct, which fussy people would remark on.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantic people who fuss over tiny distinctions are known for this excessive quibbling.

clue.text: Noble ordered handy MG? It is seen as arrogant

parts.note: high, as in high-born, means noble

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A nobleman orders a convenient MG sports car and is thought haughty.
explanation.walkthrough: MG is a British sports car make.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving with self-important superiority is the idiom used for haughty people.

clue.text: Umpires not prepared for fresh start

indicators.note: prepared means the letters are made ready in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Officials who are not ready cause play to begin again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not prepared' looks like a phrase; 'not' is fodder and 'prepared' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A restarting after a pause, such as play resuming, is a new beginning.

clue.text: In East End, judge calls to get ornamental accessories

indicators.note: Cockney speech of London's East End drops the H, so the opening letter of the word for judge goes

parts.note: to hear a case is to judge it
rings means telephone calls

explanation.surface: A judge in East London receives telephone calls.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, from London's East End, traditionally drop their aitches.
explanation.definitionFit: Jewellery worn on the lobes are decorative accessories.

clue.text: Duck coming from headland following two directions

indicators.note: following means the headland comes after the directions

parts.note: E and S are the compass points east and south
a cape is a headland

explanation.surface: A duck comes away from a headland, having followed a couple of bearings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' is a verb: to dodge or evade.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a duty is to evade it, the verb sense of getting away from something.

clue.text: A number arranged to tour river in county

indicators.note: to tour means to go around, so the pieces surround the river's letter

parts.note: some means an unspecified number
set means arranged

explanation.surface: Several people plan a tour of a river in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An English shire in the south-west, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Tacit support derived from a global body?

indicators.note: derived from means the support belongs to the global body

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, is a global body, here in possessive form
aid means support

explanation.surface: Implicit backing appears to come from an international organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means understood without being spoken, so left unspoken.

clue.text: One tending to avoid team leader

definitions.meaning: someone who habitually misses things out or dodges classes
the captain of a side, especially in sport

explanation.surface: A captain who habitually dodges things.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a person who passes over things and the informal word for a captain.

clue.text: Firm with large mistake in ruin

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a lapse is a slip or mistake

explanation.surface: A company makes a big blunder and is ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin and downfall are synonyms for total failure or breakdown.

clue.text: Relate French marshal's ringing resistance

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the marshal's name surrounds the letter for resistance

parts.note: Philippe Pétain was a Marshal of France
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: An account of a French marshal surrounding the Resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resistance' suggests the wartime French Resistance, which Pétain's Vichy regime opposed.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate to something is to concern or be connected with it.

clue.text: Porters active at work in entrepreneurial area

indicators.note: at work suggests the letters are busy being rearranged

explanation.surface: Busy porters working in a business district.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of the economy run by private enterprise for profit, where entrepreneurs operate.

clue.text: Record set by old church for long period

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A record is placed by an old church for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: An era or age, a lengthy span of history.

clue.text: Element of fizz in Coke

indicators.note: of means the letters come from within the following words

explanation.surface: An ingredient of the bubbles in a fizzy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A metallic chemical element, symbol Zn.

clue.text: Rash unionist, one originally taking part in drive

indicators.note: taking part in means the pieces go inside the word for drive

parts.note: impetus is drive or momentum
U is the abbreviation for unionist, as in Ulster Unionist

indicators.note: originally means only the opening letter of the word one is used

explanation.surface: A reckless trade unionist takes part in a campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting hastily without thought is being reckless, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Measure of intelligence about artist, one ME national

indicators.note: about means the measure goes around the artist

parts.note: IQ, intelligence quotient
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An intelligence test about an artist and one Middle Eastern citizen.
explanation.walkthrough: ME is short for Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the Middle Eastern country whose capital is Baghdad.

clue.text: Standard kept by man or machine?

indicators.note: kept by means the letters are held within the following words

explanation.surface: A benchmark maintained by a person or a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A usual or expected level is the standard.

clue.text: Liable to be shot?

parts.note: shot here means photographed rather than fired at, so this describes someone who looks good in pictures

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who looks attractive in photographs is well suited to being captured by a camera.
